title: vuln-triage-and-deps-review-notes-may-2026
content:
Context and purpose:
This is a working triage doc for the May 2026 vulnerability sweep focused on runtime dependencies and container images for hosted API and Dedicated pools. Goal: capture scanner outputs, assign owners, propose remediation approach, and schedule patch SLA milestones. This doc doubles as notes for the 2026-05-05 vuln triage sync and the dependency review follow-up (action items).

Scope:
- Services in scope: hosted-api (frontend + model-proxy), dedicated-gpu-pool nodes, private-deploy control plane images, build pipelines (CI containers).
- Scanner sources: Trivy (image/os libs), Snyk (language deps), Dependabot alerts (GH), and manual SBOM review for wheel/binary deps.
- Excludes: customer-managed on-prem deployments unless they surface in internal telemetry.

High-level scanner summary (raw counts from scans):
- Trivy (images, 2026-05-02): Critical: 2, High: 14, Medium: 38, Low: 210
- Snyk (python/node deps, 2026-05-01): Critical: 0, High: 9, Medium: 27, Low: 75
- Dependabot (GH alerts, rolling view): 12 open high/urgent dependency bumps across repos

Top prioritized findings (examples, NOT exhaustive):
1) CVE-2025-3221 (openssl derivative) - image base for dedicated-gpu-pool v2.1.4
   - Detection: Trivy in pool-images/dedicated/gpu-base:2.1.4
   - Impact: RCE potential via TLS parsing; public PoC reported
   - Affected: dedicated-gpu-pool nodes (pool-a, pool-b)
   - Owner: Diego Morales (infra)
   - Remediation options: upgrade base image to 2.1.6 (vendor patch), or rebuild with backported patch.
   - SLA: Critical -> 48 hours to mitigation, 7 days to full patch rollout
   - Status: mitigation in progress (iptables outbound block for mirrored CI runners), PR to image rebuild created: PR #4237

2) SNYK-PY-2026-0012 (django package path traversal) - web-console service
   - Detection: Snyk scan, web-console:requirements.txt
   - Impact: path traversal in admin upload endpoints
   - Owner: Priya Singh (product-web)
   - Remediation: upgrade to django 4.2.8 or apply library patch; add WAF rule as short-term control
   - SLA: High -> 7 days to patch in staging, 14 days to production
   - Status: WAF rule drafted; staging upgrade scheduled for 2026-05-09

3) GH-DEPENDABOT: minimist (npm) prototype pollution (medium/high in node-worker)
   - Owner: Liam Chen (jobs)
   - Action: bump dependency, run integration tests; mark for backport to v1.x job runner
   - SLA: Medium -> 30 days

Remediation tracking (text table - update as tasks progress):
- INFSEC-873 | CVE-2025-3221 | dedicated-gpu-pool | Diego Morales | Critical | 2026-05-02 | mitigation started | PR #4237 | target rollout 2026-05-09
- INFSEC-879 | SNYK-PY-2026-0012 | web-console | Priya Singh | High | 2026-05-01 | WAF rule pending | staging upgrade 2026-05-09
- DEP-421 | minimist bump | node-worker | Liam Chen | Medium | 2026-04-28 | open | PR linked to CI

Patch SLAs and justification (proposal):
- Critical: 48h mitigation (compensating control) + 7d full patch. Justification: exploitability + public PoC or CVSS >= 9.0.
- High: 7d staging patch, 14d prod. Justification: elevated risk, requires QA.
- Medium: 30d review and plan (backport if in supported branch).
- Low: maintain backlog, roll into regular dependency sprints.
Notes: SLA clock starts when vuln is triaged and owner assigned. If RBAC v2 approval is required for production patches (see below), include time for the approval gate into SLA if not automated.

RBAC v2 / Approval workflow impacts:
- Under RBAC v2, production image rebuilds and deploys require approvals from both infra-owner and platform-security role for dedicated/private images.
- Action: Add an exemption process for urgent Critical fixes to allow expedited deploy (auto-approve if INFSEC label + two approvers from the approved responder list).
- TODO: Draft RBAC v2 exemption flow and template for emergency patches (owner: Elena Park, due 2026-05-12).

Dependency review notes (manual SBOM checks):
- Observed several wheels with binary extensions built against glibc 2.28 on images targeting 2.33; risk of CVE surface when combined with image base issues.
- Suggestion: standardize on builder images that match target glibc, and publish SBOM per image to S3 bucket.
- Action item: Liam to add SBOM generation step into build pipeline for all public images (ticket created).

Evidence automation and SIEM export checklist (what we want):
- For every remediation: capture build artifact id, image digest, PR link, deploy job id, and signed attestations.
- Evidence store: s3://redwood-inference-evidence/patches/YYYY-MM-DD/<ticket>
- Automation hooks: after deploy-success, run evidence pipeline to snapshot audit logs + SBOM + conftools attest.
- SIEM export: enrich events with fields: service_name, image_digest, vulnerability_id, severity, remediation_ticket, deploy_job_id, approver_ids. Output format: newline-delimited JSON (NDJSON) with timestamp and trace_id.
- Action: Diego + Security Ops to prototype export using Logstash -> SIEM ingest pipeline; target mapping spec (fields) in Confluence page referenced above.

Audit log schema implications:
- Need to include RBAC v2 decision metadata (approver role, approval timestamp, reason), and link to remediation evidence artifact id.
- Proposed new fields: approver_role, approval_method (UI/API/exempt), evidence_artifact_uri.

Operational mitigations and temporary controls (examples):
- WAF rules and rate-limits for exploit paths
- Network egress filtering for repos/pools with Critical kernel/CVE exposures
- Container runtime seccomp profile tighten for pools running older images

Open questions / blockers:
- Can we reduce image rebuild time for dedicated pools to <24 hours from PR merge? (infra input needed)
- Are there any downstream customers using older pinned images that we must coordinate with for private deployments? (sales/CS ask)
- Do we have capacity in SRE squad to own the emergency rollout window this weekend? (SRE on-call availability)

Next sync and immediate action items (owner -> due):
- Rebuild gpu-base image with patched openssl (Diego Morales -> 2026-05-05) [in flight]
- Draft RBAC v2 emergency exemption template (Elena Park -> 2026-05-12)
- Add SBOM upload step to image pipeline (Liam Chen -> 2026-05-14)
- Prototype SIEM NDJSON export mapping and sample ingest (Security Ops: Priya + Diego -> 2026-05-11)
- Confirm customer coordination list with CS for private deploys (Asha -> 2026-05-07)

Notes to self / meeting fragments (raw):
- "If we can't patch desktop CI images quickly, consider gating model proxy uploads"
- "Need to keep infra rollback plan tested for emergency deploys (canary -> node-evac)"

Appendix: quick commands used in triage
- trivy image --severity CRITICAL,HIGH --format json -o /tmp/trivy-hosted-api.json registry.redwood/hosted-api:latest
- snyk test --json > /tmp/snyk-web-console.json
- gh api repos/redwood-inference/platform/dependabot/alerts --jq '.[] | {id: .id, dependency: .dependency.package.name, severity: .security_advisory.severity}'

End of working notes. Update this doc as tickets progress and before next vuln sync.
